districts.description: Capital city famed for Mughal culinary heritage in Old Dhaka, including slow-cooked Kacchi Biryani, flaky Bakarkhani, and rich Shahi Haleem.
Known for producing Bangladesh's prime national fruit jackfruit, crafted into sweet payesh, seasonal curries, and roasted seed snacks.
Historic ancient capital Sonargaon with rich fruit preserves (Murabba), fresh chhana sweets, and historic riverside tea culture.
Renowned for aromatic Amriti sweets dipped in cardamom syrup and sweet local plantains.
Home to Bikrampur culinary excellence, notable for century-old Bhagyakul royal dairy sweets and Bikrampur pitha.
Famous for organic date palm liquid jaggery (Jholir Gur) harvested in winter and folded into aromatic sandesh.
Undisputed birthplace of the celebrated Porabari Chomchom, coated with dried mawa and deeply infused with caramelized syrup.
Pillow-shaped jumbo sweets soaked in thickened malai and fresh wild catch from the wetlands of Nikli.
Famed date palm orchard region renowned for rich, fragrant molasses used in winter rice pudding and traditional pitha.
Known for spongy pure cow-milk Rosogolla and crunchy sesame seed brittle.
Celebrated for artisan sweetmakers utilizing authentic riverside date sap.
Historic Padma river crossing famous for golden chamcham and rich dried curd confectionery.
Traditional home of rich baked rice-cake Bibikhana pitha made with jaggery, thick coconut milk, and ghee.
Culinary jewel of southeastern Bangladesh, home to legendary spicy slow-roasted Kala Bhuna and communal feast Mezban beef.

districts.prominentDishBn: ছুরি শুঁটকি ভর্তা ও কোরাল মাছ
districts.description: World's longest sea beach accompanied by sun-dried spicy ribbon fish (Shutki) and grilled coastal catch.
The iconic national home of authentic Rasmalai by Matri Bhander, with tiny clotted cream pillows bathed in condensed milk.
Exclusive GI-tagged sweet confection crafted into small diamond bites coated in crisp crystalized sugar.
The premier capital of national fish Hilsa, where the Padma and Meghna rivers converge to yield the tastiest oily silver Hilsa.
Historic sweet treats prepared in Khondol bazaar with unmatched curd texture.
Dense, naturally set coastal buffalo milk curd served in traditional clay bowls with molasses.
Rich coconut haven, famed for paper-thin lacey egg crepe (Khola Jaal) and coconut sweets.
Hill Tracts indigenous cuisine featuring organic chicken steamed inside fresh green bamboo stalks with jungle herbs.

districts.prominentDishBn: হেজন ও কাপ্তাই লেকের তাজা মাছ
districts.description: Chakma and Marma traditional delicacies cooked with bamboo shoot, aromatic leaves, and freshly caught Kaptai lake fish.
Celebrated Bizu festive dish Pachon, made with over 30 varieties of wild mountain herbs and vegetables.

districts.prominentDishBn: কালাই রুটি ও ফজলি আমের মিষ্টান্ন
districts.description: Silk city famed for earthen-pan toasted black gram Kalai Ruti served with smoked eggplant and fiery chili paste.
Internationally celebrated red-clay pottery sweet curd, caramelized to silky perfection using Gauripara artisanal methods.

districts.prominentDishBn: পাবনার প্যারা ও খাঁটি ঘিয়ের সন্দেশ
districts.description: Milk belt of northern Bengal, creating dense melt-in-mouth milk Peda and unadulterated cow ghee.
Artisanal cow milk cheese wheel (Ponir) aged naturally, a staple for traditional bakeries and snacks.
Famed heritage dessert of fresh un-cooked chhana infused with light sugar syrup, originating from the Natore Rajbari royal kitchens.
Pahar-pur heritage district producing exquisite condensed milk peda and aromatic Miniket rice.
The mango capital of Bangladesh, coupled with the dense, golden Shibganj Chomchom.
Wood-apple nectar and seasonal rural pithas prepared with fresh winter harvest.
Famed culinary trademark using Piper chaba (Chui Jhal) vine stems cooked into intensely fragrant, spicy mutton.

districts.prominentDishBn: সুন্দরবনের খাঁটি মধু ও কাঁকড়া ভুনা
districts.description: Gateway to mangrove Sundarbans, known for wild mangrove blossom honey treats and spicy coastal mud crab.
Pure coastal cow milk sandesh and world-class freshwater jumbo prawns (Golda Chingri).

districts.prominentDishBn: জামতলার মিষ্টি ও নলেন পাটালি গুড়
districts.description: Pioneering home of date palm jaggery (Patali Gur) and the famed century-old Jamtola sweets.
Rich agricultural belt noted for fresh date sap winter festivals and traditional chhana creations.
Traditional artisanal confectionery crafters making airy batasa and festive sugar figurines.

districts.prominentDishBn: ছিট রুটি ও দেশি চিতল মাছ
districts.description: River Chitra delicacies including perforated rice-flour Chhit Ruti and flavorful clown knifefish curry.
Lalon Shah's mystic land, celebrated for paper-crisp sesame brittle (Tiler Khaja) and creamy pistachio Kulfi.
Layered milk-skin (Sar) delicacies fried and soaked in delicate saffron syrup.
Historic Mujibnagar district with century-old Sabitri sweet, famous for keeping freshness for weeks without cooling.

districts.prominentDishBn: বালাম চালের ভাত ও ইলিশ ভাপা
districts.description: Granary of Bengal, famous for sweet aromatic Balam rice and steaming mustard Hilsa (Ilish Bhapa).
Island district famed across Bengal for thick curd set in wild hogla-leaf wrapped clay containers from grass-fed buffaloes.

districts.prominentDishBn: ভাসমান বাজারের পেয়ারা ও ছানার মিষ্টি
districts.description: Home of the picturesque floating guava markets and fresh dairy sweets prepared along the canal banks.
Famous for hog plum (Amra) preserves and coconut-infused river delta pitha.
Coastal river catches simmered in pungent spicy Chui wood and mustard oil.

districts.prominentDishBn: কুয়াকাটার সামুদ্রিক মাছ ও শুঁটকি পাতুরি
districts.description: Daughter of the Sea (Kuakata), offering roasted marine fish and banana-leaf wrapped dried fish paturi.

districts.prominentDishBn: সাতকড়া গরুর মাংস ও নুনর পিঠা
districts.description: Aromatic citrus paradise, world-famous for tangy wild citrus Shatkora beef curry and savory Nunor pitha.

districts.prominentDishBn: সাত রঙের চা ও মণিপুরি পিঠা
districts.description: Tea capital Sreemangal, world renowned for the multi-layered Seven-Color Tea and indigenous Manipuri rice pastries.
Vast ecological wetland Tanguar Haor, celebrated for wild Boal, Pabda, and Rui fish curries cooked with indigenous greens.

districts.prominentDishBn: বিপুলের চা ও হাওরের হাঁসের মাংস
districts.description: Rolling tea gardens, spiced tea blends, and winter-special Haor duck curry with garlic and black pepper.
Home of fibreless juicy Haribhanga mangoes and Northern delicacy Shidol (fermented fish paste with taro).

districts.prominentDishBn: কাটারিভোগ চালের পোলাও ও বেদানা লিচু
districts.description: Producers of supreme aromatic Kataribhog grain and succulent sweet Bedana litchis.
Northern tip with Himalayan vista, boasting organic plainland teas and hearty claypot poultry curries.
Traditional winter cuisine featuring fiery crushed Shidol and tender steamed rice dumplings.
Legendary regional dessert featuring mini golden chhana globes bathed in reduced cardamom-scented malai.
Brahmaputra river delta treats including thick milk skin sweets and freshly caught char fish.

districts.prominentDishBn: সিদল ভাপা ও তিস্তার বৈরালী মাছ
districts.description: Teesta river delicacies, famous for tiny sparkling Bairali fish and steamed spicy Shidol.

districts.prominentDishBn: সৈয়দপুরের গরুর কাবাব ও পেঠা মিষ্টি
districts.description: Saidpur railway town famous for melt-in-mouth spiced beef seekh kebabs and heritage ash-gourd sweets.
Two-century-old royal confection created by Gopal Pal in 1824, consisting of pure curd and sugar patted into flat discs.
Exquisite needlecraft and sweet preserves (Morobba) prepared with melon, wax gourd, and sugar.
Invented by confectioner Goyanath Ghosh over a century ago; giant pillow-shaped sweets soaked in thick cream.
Garo hillside foothills district renowned for rich chhana payesh pudding and roasted sesame pithas.

categories.description: Rich biryanis, mezban curries, and regional rice delicacies
Heritage mishti, curd, and seasonal handmade pithas
Century-old heritage recipes passed through generations
Famous bazaar snacks, chotpoti, fuchka, and street kebabs
Bakarkhani, savory chanachur, and evening tea companions
Cooling puddings, kulfi, firni, and sweet curd
Seven-color tea, matha, borhani, and fresh fruit sherbets

foods.shortDescription: বগুড়ার ঐতিহ্যবাহী লালচে মিষ্টি দই, যা পোড়ামাটির সানকিতে ঘন খাঁটি দুধ ও ক্যারামেল দিয়ে ফারমেন্ট করে প্রস্তুত করা হয়।
foods.detailedDescription: বগুড়ার মিষ্টি দই বাংলাদেশের অন্যতম ভৌগোলিক নির্দেশক (GI) স্বীকৃত ঐতিহ্যবাহী খাদ্য। খাঁটি গরুর দুধ দীর্ঘক্ষণ জ্বাল দিয়ে ঘন করে তাতে চিনির ক্যারামেল ও প্রাকৃতিক বীজ দই মিশিয়ে পোড়ামাটির পাত্রে তৈরি করা হয়। মাটির পাত্র অতিরিক্ত পানি চুষে নেওয়ায় দই অত্যন্ত ঘন ও সুস্বাদু হয়।
foods.originHistory: ঊনবিংশ শতাব্দীর শুরুর দিকে বগুড়ার শেরপুরের ঘোষ পরিবারের হাত ধরে বগুড়ার দইয়ের উৎপত্তি ও খ্যাতি বিস্তৃত হয়, যা পরবর্তীতে গৌড় গোপাল ঘোষের মাধ্যমে দেশজোড়া খ্যাতি অর্জন করে।
foods.originSource: Department of Patents, Designs and Trademarks (GI Registry) & বগুড়া জেলা প্রশাসন
citationSources: Department of Patents, Designs and Trademarks (DPDT) GI Registry #7
Bogra District Administration Cultural Heritage Records
foods.imageCaption: বগুড়ার ঐতিহ্যবাহী লাল মিষ্টি দইয়ের মাটির পাত্র (Bogurar Mishti Doi in clay pot)

foods.shortDescription: Slow-cooked marinated mutton and fragrant chinigura rice infused with saffron, ghee, and potatoes.
foods.detailedDescription: Kacchi Biryani is the crown jewel of Old Dhaka's culinary tradition. Raw spiced mutton is marinated in yogurt, raw papaya paste, and fragrant spices, then layered directly with half-cooked chinigura rice and golden-fried potatoes inside a sealed handi (copper or clay pot) and slow-cooked over smoldering coals (dum). Served alongside crisp shami kebab, boiled egg, and tangy borhani.
foods.originHistory: Introduced to Bengal during the Mughal Subahdar governance in the 17th century and perfected by hereditary Ustads in Nazira Bazar and Lalbagh.
foods.originSource: Bangla Academy Folk Culinary Heritage Records
citationSources: Bangla Academy Folk Culinary Heritage Records

foods.shortDescription: Crisp, multi-layered flaky round flatbread with subtle sesame and ghee aroma.
foods.detailedDescription: Bakarkhani is a crisp, layered flatbread prepared in traditional clay tandoors across Chawkbazar and Lalbagh. The dough is rolled repeatedly with layers of ghee or dalda and flour, dusted with nigella or sesame seeds, and baked on the inner walls of the tandoor. It is commonly enjoyed for breakfast dipped in spiced milk tea or alongside sweet semolina halwa.
foods.originHistory: Associated with the tragic romance between general Aga Baker and dancer Khani Begum during the Nawab era of Dhaka.
foods.originSource: Dacca: A Record of its Changing Fortunes (A.H. Dani)
citationSources: Dacca: A Record of its Changing Fortunes (A.H. Dani)

foods.shortDescription: Tender desi chicken drumsticks gently braised in yogurt, aromatic ghee, and Kalijira rice.
foods.detailedDescription: Shahi Morog Polao features aromatic Kalijira aromatic rice, rich cow milk ghee, sour yogurt, and golden roasted onions (beresta) gently infused with whole green chillies and roasted chicken. Famous heritage shops like Nanna Biryani have served this dish for decades.
foods.originHistory: Royal Dacca household banquets during British and Mughal administrations.

foods.shortDescription: The king of sweets: caramel-toned spongy chhana cylinders rolled in delicate mawa crumbs.
foods.detailedDescription: Originating from the village of Porabari beside the Dhaleshwari river in Tangail, this sweet has an unmistakable reddish-brown outer crust, a tender honeycomb spongy center soaked in thickened cardamom sugar syrup, and a generous coating of grated dry mawa.
foods.originHistory: Pioneered in the mid-19th century by master sweetmaker Dasharath Gour using sweet water from the Dhaleshwari river.

foods.shortDescription: Intensely caramelized slow-roasted spicy black beef packed with aromatic spices.
foods.detailedDescription: Kala Bhuna is prepared by searing and slow-cooking prime cuts of beef with fried onions, mustard oil, black cardamom, star anise, radhuni, and crushed peppercorns until the meat juices evaporate and the spices cling to the meat as a deep ebony-black glaze without burning. The texture is crispy outside yet supremely tender and juicy inside.
foods.originHistory: Developed through indigenous slow-cooking methods in Chittagong port kitchens and family feasts.

foods.shortDescription: Spicy, fiery communal beef curry prepared with special Mezban masala blend and chana dal.
foods.detailedDescription: Mezban is an age-old Chittagonian socio-cultural tradition of hosting grand community feasts. The beef is stewed in huge iron cauldrons (dekchi) over open firewood flames, flavoured with a distinct aromatic masala consisting of nutmeg, mace, fennel, and white mustard seeds. Served along with steaming white rice and aromatic split Bengal gram (Chana Dal).
foods.originHistory: Dating back hundreds of years as a customary feast commemorating momentous community and religious occasions.

foods.shortDescription: Bite-sized velvety chhana pillows steeped in rich, cardamom-scented clotted condensed milk.
foods.detailedDescription: Matri Bhander of Manoharpur, Cumilla, established in 1906, is the gold standard for Rasmalai. Unlike larger versions elsewhere, authentic Cumilla Rasmalai features bite-sized mini rasgullas simmered for hours in sweetened milk until it reduces to half its volume into an indulgent, velvety malai (clotted cream).
foods.originHistory: Created by brothers Khanindra Sen and Manindra Sen in 1906 at Manoharpur in Cumilla town.

foods.shortDescription: GI-tagged caramelized red sweet curd fermented to creamy perfection in earthenware pots.
foods.detailedDescription: Bogura Mishti Doi is an iconic Bangladeshi dessert recognized with Geographical Indication (GI) status. Full-fat cow milk is boiled with sugar and reduced until it takes on a warm golden caramel tint. It is poured into unglazed porous earthenware cups (shorap/shanki), seeded with a culture, and wrapped overnight. The porous clay absorbs extra water, resulting in a thick, velvety curd.
foods.originHistory: Introduced by the Ghosh family of Sherpur in Bogura during the early 19th century, later popularized by Gour Gopal Ghosh in Gauripara.
foods.originSource: Department of Patents, Designs and Trademarks (GI Registry)
citationSources: Department of Patents, Designs and Trademarks (GI Registry)

foods.nameBn: রাজশাহীর কালাই রুটি ও বেগুন ভর্তা
foods.shortDescription: Rustic pan-toasted black gram flatbread served with fiery green chili and smoked eggplant mash.
foods.detailedDescription: Kalai Ruti is a traditional flatbread native to Rajshahi and Chapai Nawabganj made from a blend of mashkalai (black gram flour) and atap rice flour. Expert makers pat the dough entirely with bare hands over a curved clay skillet (tawa) without a rolling pin. Served piping hot with smoked eggplant mash (begun bhorta), green chili onion paste, and mustard oil.
foods.originHistory: Traditional winter staple of agrarian communities across the Barind tract.

foods.shortDescription: Pure soft chhana crumbs tossed in fragrant sugar syrup, wrapped in dried milk skin.
foods.detailedDescription: Unlike rounded sweets, Kachagolla is soft, granular, melt-in-the-mouth sweetened fresh chhana. It was accidentally created when a confectioner had leftover unsold milk curd and tossed it into boiling sugar syrup to prevent spoiling. The resulting lightly sweetened confection earned immediate royal acclaim from Rani Bhabani of Natore Rajbari.
foods.originHistory: Accidentally invented around 1760 in Madhusudan Pal's sweet shop during the reign of Rani Bhabani.

foods.shortDescription: Signature southern delicacy with tender mutton braised with pungent piper chaba woody vine.
foods.detailedDescription: Chui Jhal (Piper chaba) is a climbing herbal vine native to the southern delta. The thick woody stem is sliced into small sticks and simmered slowly with mutton, whole garlic bulbs, and mustard oil. The wood releases a spicy, numbing warmth, distinct from black pepper and chili, rendering the mutton fragrant and succulent.
foods.originHistory: Indigenous spice tradition of the lower Gangetic basin, popularized by Chuknagar and Abbas Hotel in Khulna.

foods.shortDescription: Wafer-thin crisp sesame seed brittle with delicate airy honeycomb layers.
foods.detailedDescription: Tiler Khaja is a light, crunchy sweet made by boiling sugar and cardamom into a thick candy, pulling and folding the aerated candy into ribbons, and coating with toasted white sesame seeds. It snaps crisply with every bite.
foods.originHistory: Originated in Kushtia town during the British era by sweetmaker families of Mohini Mills quarter.

foods.shortDescription: Tender beef curry infused with the aromatic, tangy rind of wild mountain citrus Shatkora.
foods.detailedDescription: Shatkora (Citrus macroptera) is a semi-wild citrus fruit native to the forested hills of Sylhet and Assam. Thick slices of the fruit's aromatic peel are cooked into beef or mutton gravy. The natural bitter-sour oils impart a fragrant citrus aroma and robust tang that cuts through the richness of the meat.
foods.originHistory: Centuries-old tribal and Bengali hill culinary integration in the Surma and Kushiyara river valleys.

foods.shortDescription: World-famous multi-colored tea glass exhibiting distinct layers of black, green, and milk brews.
foods.detailedDescription: Invented in Sreemangal by Romesh Ram Gour at Nilkantha Tea Cabin, this beverage features up to seven distinct horizontal colored layers in a single clear glass. Each layer has varying densities, tea extracts, milk concentrations, and spice balances that stay separated as you sip.
foods.originHistory: Invented by Romesh Ram Gour at Nilkantha Tea Cabin in 2002.
foods.originSource: Bangladesh Tea Board & National Tourism Documentation
citationSources: Bangladesh Tea Board & National Tourism Documentation

foods.nameBn: চাঁদপুরের রূপালি ইলিশ পাতুরি ও ঝোল
foods.shortDescription: Steamed Hilsa steaks coated in ground mustard and green chilies wrapped in charred banana leaves.
foods.detailedDescription: Chandpur is the national hub where the Padma and Meghna rivers converge, yielding the prized oily, sweet silver Hilsa. In Paturi, thick fillets are marinated in cold-pressed mustard oil, ground black and yellow mustard seeds, green chilies, and turmeric, wrapped in banana leaves, and pan-roasted on low flame until tender and smoky.
foods.originHistory: Heritage riverine delicacy of the Meghna delta fishermen communities.

foods.shortDescription: Two-century-old royal confection of pure chhana discs patted on parchment paper.
foods.detailedDescription: Muktagachar Monda dates back to 1824 when Gopal Pal presented it to Maharaja Suryakanta Acharya Chowdhury. It is prepared using only pure unpasteurized cow chhana and unrefined sugar cooked over low heat, hand-flattened into thick discs, and preserved on paper. It contains no artificial flavors or preservatives.
foods.originHistory: Invented in 1824 by Ram Gopal Pal under the patronage of the Muktagacha Zamindars.

foods.shortDescription: Pillow-sized jumbo spongy mishti soaked in condensed cardamom malai.
foods.detailedDescription: Balish (literally "pillow") Mishti was conceptualized by sweetmaker Goyanath Ghosh of Netrakona in the early 20th century. Sized from standard to grand pillow shapes, the sweet is made of kneaded chhana, boiled in syrup, and coated in thick, reduced malai before serving.
foods.originHistory: Crafted by master sweetmaker Goyanath Ghosh around 1900 in Netrakona town.

foods.nameBn: বরিশালের ইলিশ ভাপা ও বালাম চাল
foods.shortDescription: Steamed Hilsa in mustard yogurt sauce over heirloom aromatic Balam rice.
foods.detailedDescription: Barishal, known as the granary of Bengal, is famous for its heirloom Balam rice, an aromatic medium grain. In Ilish Bhapa, fresh river hilsa is coated with pungent stone-ground mustard paste, mustard oil, sour curd, and slit green chilies, steamed in a sealed tiffin box.
foods.originHistory: Traditional riverside cooking practice of southern river deltas.

foods.shortDescription: Dense, naturally set organic buffalo curd served with fresh date palm syrup.
foods.detailedDescription: Bhola island in the Bay of Bengal estuary is home to thousands of free-range buffaloes grazing on the coastal sandbars (chars). Raw buffalo milk has higher fat and solids, so it sets naturally into an ultra-thick, creamy white curd in clay pots without any artificial thickeners. Best enjoyed with winter date palm liquid jaggery.
foods.originHistory: Centuries of indigenous pastoral farming in the Meghna estuary chars.

foods.shortDescription: Spicy fermented fish paste mashed with taro stems, garlic, and dried red chilies.
foods.detailedDescription: Shidol is an indigenous fermented fish preparation crafted across northern Bangladesh. Tiny mola or punti fish are cleaned, dried in the sun, blended with mashed taro stem (kochu) and turmeric, shaped into cakes, and sun-dried and fermented in earthen pots. Roasted and mashed with fiery red chili and mustard oil.
foods.originHistory: Ancient preservation method developed by rural communities of North Bengal.

foods.shortDescription: Aromatic long-grain heirloom rice cooked with golden fried shallots and ghee.
foods.detailedDescription: Kataribhog rice from Dinajpur has a distinct dagger-curved tip (Katari) and an irresistible floral aroma. Prepared into a royal white polao infused with clarified butter, whole cardamom, bay leaf, and roasted cashews.
foods.originHistory: Harvested in the fertile red soils of Dinajpur for royal households of Bengal.

foods.shortDescription: GI-certified bite-sized crisp sugar-frosted sweet curd diamonds.
foods.detailedDescription: Chanar Mukhi is prepared by pressing fresh chhana into firm blocks, cutting them into tiny cubic or diamond dice, boiling them in clear sugar syrup, and tossing until a crunchy white sugary crust crystallizes over each piece. Recognized as a Geographical Indication (GI) product of Bangladesh.
foods.originHistory: Originated in the late 19th century by master sweetmaker Kashiram Das in Brahmanbaria town.

foods.shortDescription: Spicy sun-cured ribbon fish mashed with charred onions, garlic, and fiery Naga chillies.
foods.detailedDescription: Sun-dried ribbon fish (Chhuri Shutki) caught off the Bay of Bengal coastline, roasted on dry charcoal grates to intensify umami, shredded, and pounded in stone mortars with roasted whole garlic, red onions, and hot mustard oil.
foods.originHistory: Coastal fishermen culinary culture of Nazirtek, the largest shutki drying yard in Asia.

foods.shortDescription: Country chicken marinated in mountain ginger and wrapped in wild bamboo cooked over coals.
foods.detailedDescription: An indigenous culinary masterpiece from the Hill Tracts. Free-range chicken is marinated with mountain turmeric, wild ginger, bird's eye chili, and hill spices, packed into green bamboo hollows, sealed with banana leaves, and cooked slowly over wood embers.
foods.originHistory: Traditional forest and jungle survival cooking of Marma and Bawm indigenous communities.

foods.shortDescription: Century-old juicy syrup-soaked sweet with velvety smooth chhana texture.
foods.detailedDescription: Crafted since 1955 under the shade of a jam (blackberry) tree at Jamtola bazaar by SK Sadhu Ghosh. Prepared from pure cow milk and soaked in mild, fragrant sugar syrup that melts in the mouth.
foods.originHistory: Founded in 1955 by sweetmaker SK Sadhu Ghosh in Jamtola bazaar.

foods.shortDescription: Golden chhana balls swimming in rich, creamy reduced milk with saffron highlights.
foods.detailedDescription: Rasmanjari of Gaibandha was established in 1948 by Ramesh Chandra Ghosh. Small, perfectly rounded chhana globes are fried lightly or poached in sugar syrup and steeped in thickened milk reduced slowly over firewood.
foods.originHistory: Pioneered in 1948 by Ramesh Chandra Ghosh of Gaibandha.

foods.shortDescription: Naturally aged pure cow milk cheese wheels with mild savory aroma.
foods.detailedDescription: Sirajganj, situated in the milk-rich Chalan Beel catchment area, is the historical cradle of Bangladeshi artisanal cheese (Ponir). Made by curdling fresh cow milk, pressing whey through muslin cloths into wooden molds, and salting to cure naturally.
foods.originHistory: Introduced by Portuguese settlers in Bengal during the 16th century and naturalized by local Ghopa communities.

foods.shortDescription: Rich baked winter cake made with liquid date jaggery, thick coconut milk, and rice flour.
foods.detailedDescription: Bibikhana Pitha is a cherished festive baked rice cake from Shariatpur and Faridpur. Prepared with stone-ground rice flour, concentrated coconut cream, fresh date palm jaggery (nolen gur), and a hint of cardamom, slow-baked with coals on top and bottom.
foods.originHistory: Heritage aristocratic Muslim household winter confection of the lower Padma basin.
foods.originSource: Folk Pitha Archives of Greater Faridpur
citationSources: Folk Pitha Archives of Greater Faridpur

foods.nameBn: নোয়াখালীর খোলাজা পিঠা ও নারকেল নাড়ু
foods.shortDescription: Delicate lace crepe baked on clay skillet accompanied by spicy duck curry and sweet coconut truffles.
foods.detailedDescription: Kholajaal is an ultra-thin, netted crepe baked without oil on an unglazed earthen pan (khola) made from liquid rice batter and eggs. It takes barely 30 seconds to cook, producing a soft mesh that soaks up spicy duck curry.
foods.originHistory: Coastal culinary heritage of Noakhali families.

foods.nameEn: Haor Fresh Boal & Chitol Fish Curry
foods.nameBn: হাওরের তাজা বোয়াল ও চিতল মাছের ঝোল
foods.shortDescription: Wild wetland giant fish simmered with tomato, green coriander, and mustard.
foods.detailedDescription: Tanguar and Hakaluki Haors produce some of Bengal's most sought-after freshwater wild fish. Tender steaks of Boal or Chitol are cooked in light broth with tomatoes, slit chillies, and freshly crushed spices.
foods.originHistory: Traditional haor delta fishermen cooking traditions.

foods.nameEn: Sundarbans Wild Honey & Mud Crab Curry
foods.nameBn: সুন্দরবনের খাঁটি মধু ও কাদা কাঁকড়া ভুনা
foods.shortDescription: Fresh mangrove forest mud crab simmered in coconut milk, garlic, and wild Khalisha flower honey.
foods.detailedDescription: Harvested from the mangrove wilderness of the Sundarbans, large mud crabs are cooked in a savory curry spiced with cumin, dried red chili, coconut cream, and glazed lightly with raw mangrove blossom honey.
foods.originHistory: Coastal lifestyle of the Mouwal (honey collectors) and Bawali woodsmen of the Sundarbans.

foods.nameBn: জামালপুরের চালকুমড়ার মোরব্বা ও পুলি পিঠা
foods.shortDescription: Translucent, crystal-glazed candied wax gourd bites infused with cardamom and rosewater.
foods.detailedDescription: Traditional Morobba of Jamalpur is made from mature ash gourd (chalkumra), carefully pricked, lime-water treated, and stewed in thick clarified sugar syrup until crystalline and translucent.
foods.originHistory: Traditional artisanal confectionery heritage along the Old Brahmaputra riverbanks.

foods.nameBn: সাতক্ষীরার গলদা চিংড়ি মালাইকারি ও সন্দেশ
foods.shortDescription: Freshwater jumbo prawns cooked in rich coconut cream paired with fresh chhana sandesh.
foods.detailedDescription: Satkhira boasts vast estuaries producing the country's finest giant freshwater prawns (Golda Chingri). Cooked into an authentic Malaikari with fresh grated coconut milk, ghee, and whole spices.
foods.originHistory: Estuarine coastal culinary heritage of southwestern Bengal.

foods.shortDescription: Dry caramelized sweet known for lasting weeks at room temperature without preservatives.
foods.detailedDescription: Sabitri is an ingenious heritage sweet developed in Meherpur town over 150 years ago by Vasudeva Saha. Made from dried chhana and caramelized milk solids, it retains its flavor for weeks without refrigeration.
foods.originHistory: Created in 1861 by Vasudeva Saha in Meherpur town.

foods.shortDescription: Rich golden sweet with deep mawa fragrance and dense cottage cheese core.
foods.detailedDescription: Shibganj Chomchom in Chapai Nawabganj has been crafted for over a century. Simmered in caramelized sugar syrup until deep amber-brown, dusted with toasted dry milk crumbles.
foods.originHistory: Artisanal sweetmakers of Shibganj bazaar dating back to the 1920s.

foods.shortDescription: Signature soft and juicy regional sweet prepared with fresh local dairy.
foods.detailedDescription: Originated in Khondol market of Parshuram upazila in Feni. Master confectioners use whole cow milk to make delicately textured chhana balls soaked in fragrant warm cardamom syrup.
foods.originHistory: Century-old bazaar heritage in Parshuram, Feni.

foods.shortDescription: Coastal sun-dried marine fish steamed in banana leaves with green mustard sauce.
foods.detailedDescription: Kuakata's sea coast provides diverse marine fish like Loitta and Rupchanda. Sun-cured dried fish is mashed with mustard, green chilies, garlic cloves, folded into charred banana leaf packets, and griddled.
foods.originHistory: Coastal Rakhine and Bengali artisanal fishermen cuisine.

foods.shortDescription: Condensed milk fudge discs prepared by slow-stirring pure cow milk over wood heat.
foods.detailedDescription: Pabna is the milk capital of Bangladesh, home to the largest dairy cooperative societies. Pabna Peda is crafted by simmering pure cow milk for hours into dense mawa paste, hand-molded into discs with embossed stamps.
foods.originHistory: Traditional pastoral dairy heritage in Santhia and Chatmohar of Pabna.

foods.shortDescription: Royal Bikrampur heritage sweets made from cow chhana and golden date syrup.
foods.detailedDescription: Bhagyakul in Bikrampur (Munshiganj) was historically known for its royal estates and grand banquets. Confectioners in Bhagyakul create delicate chhana sweets cooked in aromatic winter jaggery.
foods.originHistory: Royal patronages under the Bhagyakul Roy family in the 19th century.

userFoods.notes: Unbelievably tender mutton with melt-in-the-mouth potato. The aroma of saffron and ghee is unbeatable!
Smoky, intensely spiced beef with crisp outer bark. Best with hot tandoori ruti.
Pure heaven in an earthen cup. Caramelized sweetness without any artificial aftertaste.
Tasted directly in Porabari, Tangail. Fragrant mawa and deep caramelized syrup!
Tasted directly in Porabari, Tangail. Fragrant mawa and deep caramelized syrup!

foodReviews.comment: Authentic Old Dhaka kacchi biryani has a distinct richness you simply cannot replicate anywhere else.
Spices cling to the meat perfectly. An absolute must-eat when visiting Chittagong.
